barriers.description: Physicians and some provider professions were under-represented in the sample, likely because busy clinical schedules reduced engagement in voluntary research.
barriers.justification: This recruitment bias limited the researchers' ability to manage comprehensive user understanding and to facilitate involvement from all relevant provider types, constraining the representativeness of feedback used to specify requirements and plan implementation.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Nearly 40% of the sample were psychologists, and as such other professions may be under represented in the current study, possibly due to that physicians busy schedules may reduce engagement in voluntary research studies.

barriers.description: Participants only received the draft RISE manual to review if they had time and were given up to 20 minutes during the interview to review it.
barriers.justification: Constrained participant preparation time impeded the researchers' ability to elicit deep, informed feedback and to evaluate the intervention thoroughly, limiting the quality of user understanding and design evaluation.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Prior to the interview, participants received the draft RISE manual to review if time permitted.

barriers.description: Undue influences such as social desirability may have affected provider responses to study team members.
barriers.justification: Social desirability and related interpersonal response biases hindered researchers' ability to obtain candid user feedback, reducing the validity of insights used to integrate feedback and iterate on the design.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Additionally, it is possible that other undue influences (e.g., social desirability) may have impacted provider response to study team members about the RISE intervention.

barriers.description: The study did not formally assess providers' level of training or experience with IPV.
barriers.justification: Omitting measurement of provider IPV experience reduced the researchers' ability to characterize user subgroups and to translate nuanced user knowledge into precise requirements and targeted training design.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Further, the current study did not formerly assess for provider’s level of training in or experience with IPV, which may have influenced results.

barriers.description: Data collection was limited to two VHA medical centers in the New England region, constraining regional and system diversity of informants.
barriers.justification: Restricted geographic/site scope limited researchers' ability to understand broader contexts of use and to generalize findings across varied implementation settings, impeding context-driven design decisions.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Providers interviewed in this study work at VA Healthcare Systems in the New England region of the US, and therefore findings may be specific to these regions and healthcare systems.

barriers.description: Some participants reported that IPV interventions were not perceived as a priority by clinics, the healthcare system, or leadership.
barriers.justification: Organizational lack of prioritization by external stakeholders constrained researchers' ability to plan feasible implementation strategies, to facilitate provider involvement, and to secure support needed for iterative testing in routine care.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Some participants expressed that an IPV intervention was not perceived as a priority by the clinic, the healthcare system, and/or the leadership.

barriers.description: Providers identified limited time, resources, and physical space in primary care and other busy clinical settings as barriers to delivering RISE.
barriers.justification: Clinical workload and setting constraints hindered the researchers' ability to evaluate and iterate the intervention in fast-paced primary care contexts and impeded eliciting realistic implementation feasibility data from users.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Participants identified several potential barriers to implementing RISE. Participants also identified barriers such as the limited time, resources, and space available in primary care and other busy clinical settings.
